title: Isaac Hite of Cave Spring
summary: Isaac Hite came to Kentucky with Thomas Bullitt's 1773 surveyors, helped found Harrodsburg, was wounded at Boonesborough in 1777, and built Cave Spring, a mill-and-tannery farm east of the Falls, where he died in 1794.
bodyMarkdown:
In the summer of 1773 [Isaac Hite](/people/#isaac-hite), a Virginian of about 20, came down the Ohio to join one of the first surveying parties sent into the Kentucky country. Twenty-one years later he died on a farm he had carved out of that same ground, a few miles east of the Falls of the Ohio. In between, he took part in almost every stage of Kentucky's founding.

## With Bullitt at the Falls

Hite was [born in 1753 in Hampshire County, Virginia](https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/c9c1bd3d-0d01-44e1-9325-07be21b6b36f/). In 1773 he joined [Thomas Bullitt](/people/#thomas-bullitt)'s party, which [surveyed the land at the Falls](/stories/capt-thomas-bullitts-1773-survey-party/) where Louisville now stands and much of what became Jefferson County. Land Office records list him as a [deputy surveyor for Fincastle County](https://www.sos.ky.gov/land/resources/articles/Documents/articleearlykysurveyors.pdf) from that year.

## Harrodsburg and Boonesborough

He came back in 1774, the year [James Harrod's party laid out the town](https://grokipedia.com/page/Harrodsburg,_Kentucky), and [helped establish Harrodsburg](https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/c9c1bd3d-0d01-44e1-9325-07be21b6b36f/), and he lived there until about 1781, running surveys across the new settlements. In 1775 the Boiling Spring settlement sent him as a delegate to the Transylvania convention at Boonesborough, the first attempt to set up a government in Kentucky.

Two years later he was inside Boonesborough's stockade when it came under attack. The [state marker for his home](https://history.ky.gov/markers/isaac-hites-home) says he fought beside [Daniel Boone](/people/#daniel-boone) and the other defenders and was wounded on April 24, 1777. He later served under [George Rogers Clark](/people/#george-rogers-clark) in the campaigns of 1780 and 1782 against the Shawnee towns north of the Ohio.

## Justice and surveyor

In January 1781 the governor of Virginia named him one of the first justices of the peace for [the first county court held in Kentucky](https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/c9c1bd3d-0d01-44e1-9325-07be21b6b36f/). The surveyor's chain kept him busy too. He worked as a deputy surveyor in Kentucky, Lincoln, Jefferson, Fayette and Nelson counties between 1780 and 1792, and every line he ran helped settle who owned the new country.

## Cave Spring

His own claim lay on Goose Creek, east of the Falls. He called the farm Cave Spring, after a stream that ran out of a limestone cave on the property, and [built a mill and a tannery there](https://kyhi.org/asylums/central-state-hospital/). [John Filson](/people/#john-filson)'s 1784 map of Kentucke already marked the place as [Hite's Mill](https://www.cityofanchorage.org/community/history.php). Hite settled there for good in the late 1780s and married in 1788.

## A will and a death

He signed his will on February 8, 1794, and died that year at about 40. A later local history says Native raiders wounded him at Cave Spring that February and that he died soon after; his will, written weeks earlier, leaves the story uncertain. It left his widow 400 acres, including the home place, to pass in time to their son, and a daughter 500 acres nearby.

The family held the land for generations. In 1869 the state bought part of the old Hite land for a juvenile House of Reform, which opened in 1871. The grounds later became the Lakeland asylum, Central State Hospital.

## Kentucky today

A state marker for Isaac Hite's Home stands on Lucas Lane in Anchorage, and the map pin marks it. Nearby, the [Hite-Foree Log House](https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/c9c1bd3d-0d01-44e1-9325-07be21b6b36f/), a big log house with two rooms around a central chimney, is on the National Register for its tie to the Hite family, though its exact date and first owner are not known.
